title: ItemNet
tagline: An offline batch description generator and editor for the OmniSight system.
description:
ItemNet writes better clothing and armour descriptions for SkyrimNet.

SkyrimNet's OmniSight describes each item from screenshots of the item on its own. It also strips out any body mesh. Without a body for context, vision models often misread what they see: a brief floating in mid-air gets described as a "chest bandeau", and pieces of an outfit come out as unrelated objects.

ItemNet renders each item on an optional mannequin body from four sides, using your own load order:

- Your Nord race's body, hands, feet and head
- Your BodySlide meshes and skin textures
- The slot hiding the game itself applies

It then has a vision model describe the item, lets you review and edit the result, and saves it into SkyrimNet's database as a locked entry.

Includes support for:
- Bulk item describing, including multiple parallel requests, and only running one call for multiple items with the same mesh and textures (for the many enchanted variants which look identical).
- Importing your provider and models settings from SkyrimNet.
- Copy/Paste names and descriptions.
- PBR Textures.

Suggested vision models (I've tried a lot during testing, these are the ones I found the best):
- ~z-ai/glm-flash-latest (5.3 as of writing): Fast, cheap, and writes fairly well. On certain more complex things it can make mistakes, however.
- meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor: Slower, fairly cheap, and accurate. Descriptions are more bland than GLM Flash, but it can understand more things.
- anthropic/claude-opus-5.5: The heavyweight. Does an excellent job, but _very_ expensive compared to the others. Only use it on the most difficult items, and only if you can't think of how to write it yourself... unless you have a subscription and use SkyrimNet MultiProxy.
author: maeyanie
